chunks: From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Abu Yahya al-Wasiti, from one of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Indeed, behind Yemen is a valley called Wadi Barhoot, and no one crosses that valley except the black snakes and owls from the birds. In that valley is a well called Balhout, to which the souls of the polytheists are taken morning and evening; they are given drink from the water of pus. Behind that valley is a people called Al-Zareeh. When Allah the Exalted sent Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family), a cow of theirs, among them, shouted and struck with its tail, and called out to them in a clear voice: 'O children of Al-Zareeh! A man has come to Tihamah calling to the testimony that there is no god but Allah.' They said, 'What made Allah make this cow speak?' He said, so it called out to them a second time.

So they resolved to build a ship, so they built it, and seven of them embarked in it, and they carried provisions as much as Allah put into their hearts. Then they raised its sail and set it loose in the sea, and it did not cease carrying them until it cast them up at Jeddah. So they came to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), and the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said to them: 'You are the people of Al-Zareeh, among whom the calf called out?' They said, 'Yes.' They said, 'Present to us, O Messenger of Allah, the Religion and the Book.' So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) presented to them the Religion and the Book, and the Sunnah, and the Obligations, and the Laws, just as it came from Allah the Majestic and Mighty. And he appointed over them a man from the Banu Hashim whom he sent with them. So there will be no difference among them until the Hour.

key_terms.الذَّرِيحُ: Al-Zareeh, a specific people or tribe mentioned in the narrative
key_terms.بَلَهُوتُ: The well of Balhout where polytheists' souls are quenched
key_terms.بَنُو هَاشِمٍ: Banu Hashim, the clan to which the appointed guardian belonged
key_terms.مَاءِ الصَّدِيدِ: Water of pus, the drink for the souls of polytheists
key_terms.وَادِي بَرَهُوتَ: Valley of Barhoot, a geographical location behind Yemen

ai.seo_question: What is the story of the people of Al-Zareeh and their speaking cow in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi highlights the miraculous sign of the speaking calf, confirming Muhammad’s (saww) prophethood to the people of Al-Zareeh, a group who subsequently embraced Islam and were guided by a leader from Banu Hashim to maintain unity. The narrative underscores the Shia emphasis on the continuity of religious authority and the absence of division among those who accept the divine message through the Prophet and his household. It serves as a testament to the supernatural validation of the Prophet’s mission and the immediate acceptance of the true faith by those who witnessed the miracle.

en.hubeali: H 14823 – From him, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Abu Yahya Al-Wasity, from one of our companions, who has said: Abu Abdullahasws has said that; ‘Behind Al-Yemen there is a valley called Barhoot, and there is no permission to be in that valley except for the black (snakes) and the owls from the birds.

In that valley is a well called Balhout where the souls of the ‘الْمُشْرِكِينَ’ Polytheists come to feed and be quenched from the water of pus. Behind that valley are a people called Al-Zareeh. When Allah<sup>azwj</sup> the High Sent Muhammad<sup>saww</sup>, one of their cows shouted and struck with its tail. So it called out, ‘O children of Al-Zareeh!’ - in an eloquent voice – ‘There has come a man<sup>saww</sup> at Tahaamat, calling to the testimony of ‘There is no god except Allah<sup>azwj</sup>’. They said, ‘What has Made Allah<sup>azwj</sup> to Make this cow to speak?’ So it called out among them for a second time’.

So they decided to build a ship. So they built it and seven of them embarked in it, and they carried as much provisions as Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Struck them in their hearts. Then they raised its sails and floated it in the sea. They did not stop sailing in it until they reached Jeddah. So they came to the Prophet<sup>saww</sup>. The Prophet<sup>saww</sup> said to them: ‘You are the people of Al-Zareeh among whom the calf called out?’ They said, ‘Yes. O Rasool Allah<sup>saww</sup>, present to us the Religion and the Book’. So the Rasool Allah<sup>saww</sup> presented to them the Religion, and the Book, and the Sunnah, and the Obligation, and the Laws just as it had come from the presence of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Majestic and Mighty, and made a guardian over them, a man from the Clan of Hashim<sup>as</sup> who journeyed with them. So there will be no differences among them until the Hour (Day of Judgement)’.
